This widening captures the compounding effect of uncertainty — each additional time step introduces new shocks that cannot be anticipated, and those shocks accumulate. If realized volatility spikes — as it tends to during periods of market stress or major data surprises — even the short-horizon interval could prove too narrow. Model misspecification is a persistent source of risk: if the data-generating process has shifted in a way not captured by my inputs, all three forecasts could be systematically biased in the same direction, which would not be reflected in the interval widths.
